h1: Landscaping & lawn care at Lake Cherokee
lede: Lake lots slope, wash out and hold water in the wrong places. We build the walls, drains, beds and lawns that keep a Lake Cherokee yard where it belongs, from the house down toward the water.
intro: Yard Dog Landscapes handles landscaping and lawn care for homes on Lake Cherokee, a short drive southeast of our Longview base. We're family-owned, started by Miller Maines in 2017, and Miller and the same crew of four do every job. We never subcontract. We're fully insured, rated 5.0 on Google from {{REVIEWS}} reviews, and every project starts with a free walkthrough and a written, itemized estimate, usually within a day. Request a free quote anytime.

Lake lots work differently from town lots. Most yards on the lake fall toward the water, so every hard rain runs across the lawn, carries sandy topsoil with it and cuts ruts along drives and paths. Pines and hardwoods shade a lot of the ground, and grass thins out on the steeper banks where it's hard to mow. The fix is usually some mix of retaining walls, grading, drains, beds and ground cover that hold the soil in place.

In July 2026 we rebuilt a leaning block retaining wall along a Lake Cherokee driveway. We took it down, set a compacted base and put it back up course by course with drainage fabric and pipe behind it, so water has a way out instead of pushing on the block. Docks, boathouses and seawalls are not our work. We stay on the land side and handle the yard from the house down.

yard_notes.title: Slopes to the water
yard_notes.text: Most lake lots fall toward the shore, so every rain moves water and soil downhill. Grading and walls decide if that happens slowly or all at once.

yard_notes.title: Bare banks erode fast
yard_notes.text: Sandy topsoil washes quickly once the grass thins. Beds, ground cover and terraces hold a bank better than turf you can't safely mow.

yard_notes.title: Drives cut into the slope
yard_notes.text: A driveway cut into a bank puts steady pressure on whatever holds it up. Walls built without drainage behind them lean, which is exactly what we rebuilt at Lake Cherokee in July 2026.

yard_notes.title: Needles and leaves head downhill
yard_notes.text: Pines and hardwoods around the lake drop into beds, onto lawns and down the slope. Regular cleanups keep it off the grass and out of the drains.

faq.q: Do you build docks, boathouses or seawalls on Lake Cherokee?
faq.a: No. Docks, boathouses and seawalls are not our work, and you'll want a contractor who specializes in shoreline structures for those. We handle the land side: retaining walls, drainage, grading, beds, sod, mowing and cleanups.

faq.q: How much does a retaining wall cost at Lake Cherokee?
faq.a: Most retaining walls run $3,000 to $19,000, depending on height and length. Short garden walls start at a few thousand dollars, and tall structural walls on a steep bank can run $20,000 or more. We price yours after walking the slope.

faq.q: Can you stop my Lake Cherokee yard from washing out?
faq.a: Usually, with the right mix. We slow the water with grading and swales, carry it with French drains, hold steep ground with walls or terraces and cover bare soil with beds, ground cover or sod. Most drainage projects run $2,000 to $3,750.

faq.q: Do you mow and maintain lake lots too?
faq.a: Yes. We mow, trim, clean up leaves and keep beds in shape at Lake Cherokee. Banks too steep for a mower get string-trimmed, and we'll tell you where a bed or ground cover would make more sense than grass. Weekly mowing for a typical yard starts at $65 a visit, and larger lots or heavy trimming can move that number.

service_angles.lawn-maintenance: Mowing a Lake Cherokee lot means working slopes. We mow the level ground and gentle grades, string-trim the banks too steep for a mower and blow clippings back onto the lawn instead of down toward the water. Typical yards start at $65 per visit, and if a bank keeps scalping or sliding, we'll suggest turning it into a bed.
service_angles.leaf-removal: Trees around Lake Cherokee drop leaves and pine needles that slide down the slope, pile against walls, clog drains and wash toward the water. We clear the lawn, beds and drive, clean out drain inlets and haul it all away. Pricing depends on tree cover and how steep the lot is, so it's set after a walkthrough.
service_angles.fertilization: On a lake lot, fertilizer that washes off a slope ends up in the water and does the lawn no good. We soil test first, use slower-release products, keep the spreader off drives and away from the shoreline and time feedings around the forecast. Feedings start from about $190 per visit.
service_angles.hedge-trimming: Hedges on lake lots often double as screens from the road or the neighbors without blocking the view of the water. We hold them at the height you want, keep them full from the ground up and haul every clipping off instead of leaving it on the slope. Lake lot hedge jobs usually run $150 to $800.
service_angles.tree-shrub-care: Lake Cherokee yards tend to have tall pines and hardwoods with shrubs crowding underneath. We prune shrubs and small trees for shape and light, lift low limbs that block the view to the water and remove small trees and shrubs that have outgrown their spot, while large trees near the house belong to a tree service. Our part is quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.tree-planting: A new tree on a lake slope needs a level planting shelf so water soaks in instead of running past the root ball. We dig wide, build the basin up on the downhill side, mulch it and pick trees that handle wet feet low on the lot and dry ground near the top. Planting here is quoted once we've walked the slope.
service_angles.sod-installation: Sod is the fastest way to cover bare, washing ground on a gentle lake slope, because it holds soil the day it goes down. On steeper grades we pin it so it can't slide before it roots, and grass choice follows the shade under the trees. Pallet pricing puts most sod jobs between $1,500 and $4,700.
service_angles.landscaping: Landscaping at Lake Cherokee is about holding ground and framing the view. We terrace slopes with walls or boulders, plant beds and ground cover where grass won't hold and build paths toward the water that stay put after a storm. Most projects run $900 to $3,600, and a full-property Design Preview lets you see the plan before you commit.
service_angles.flower-bed-installation: On a lake lot, a bed is often the best answer for ground too steep to mow. We build beds across the slope rather than down it, edge the low side so mulch and soil stay put and plant shrubs and ground covers with roots that grip. Plant in fall or early spring and the roots get a season to grab hold before summer.
service_angles.mulch-installation: Mulch on a slope wants to wash downhill. Pine straw is usually the better choice on steep lake beds because it knits together and stays put, and shredded hardwood works on the flatter ground near the house, both laid 1 to 1.5 inches deep over a prepped bed. Lake lot bed refreshes mostly run $600 to $2,400.
service_angles.hardscaping: Patios and walkways on a lake lot have to deal with grade. We cut and fill to make level ground, build up the low side with a wall where needed and set everything on a compacted base pitched to drain, with steps down the slope for a safe way toward the water. Patio and path projects mostly run $3,100 to $9,100.
service_angles.retaining-walls: Retaining walls do the heavy lifting on a lake lot. In July 2026 we rebuilt a leaning block wall along a Lake Cherokee driveway course by course, on a compacted base with drainage fabric and pipe behind it so water drains out instead of building pressure. Walls here run $3,000 to $19,000 for most jobs, depending on height and length.
service_angles.drainage: Water on a lake lot always heads downhill, and the trick is getting it there without taking the yard along. We use swales, French drains, downspout runs and dry creek beds to slow it down and carry it past the house and down the slope on a controlled path. Small fixes start around $450, and most lake lot projects fall between $2,000 and $3,750.
service_angles.christmas-lights: Lake houses at Lake Cherokee often have long rooflines, gables and porches on both the road side and the water side. We supply the lights, custom-cut professional C9 lines to fit, install them, take them down after the season and store them. Quotes come from a photo mock-up, and most homes start at $900.
service_angles.irrigation: Lake Cherokee lots slope toward the water, and a sprinkler that runs too long just sends runoff down the bank. We zone the slope separately from the flat ground near the house, run shorter cycles, and put beds and banks on drip so the water stays where it lands.

lawn-maintenance.q: Can you mow the steep bank down to the water?
lawn-maintenance.a: If it's safe to mow, yes. Banks too steep for a mower get string-trimmed instead. If a slope keeps scalping, washing or sliding, we'll suggest a bed, ground cover or a wall so you're not fighting it every week.

leaf-removal.q: Do you keep leaves out of the lake?
leaf-removal.a: We collect leaves and haul them off site instead of blowing them downhill toward the water. We also clear drain inlets and the base of walls, where leaves pile up and block water.

fertilization.q: Is it safe to fertilize a lawn on a lake lot?
fertilization.a: Yes, when it's done carefully. We soil test so we only apply what the lawn needs, keep product off drives and away from the shoreline, and time feedings so a storm doesn't wash them off the slope.

hedge-trimming.q: Can you trim a hedge without blocking my lake view?
hedge-trimming.a: Yes. We can hold a hedge at a set height so it screens the road or a neighbor without cutting off the water. Show us where the view line is and we'll trim to it every visit.

tree-shrub-care.q: Can you open up the view to the lake?
tree-shrub-care.a: Within limits. We can lift low limbs, thin shrubs and remove small trees that block the view. Big trees and limbs high in the canopy are work for a tree service.

tree-planting.q: What trees grow well near the water at Lake Cherokee?
tree-planting.a: Bald cypress handles wet ground low on a lot well. Up the slope, native oaks do well in the open, and redbuds and dogwoods fit in the shade of existing pines. We'll match each tree to how wet or dry its spot stays.

sod-installation.q: Will sod hold on my sloped lake yard?
sod-installation.a: On a gentle slope, yes, especially once it's rooted. On steeper ground we pin it in place until the roots take. Past a certain grade, a bed or a wall will hold better than any grass.

landscaping.q: How do you landscape a lot that slopes to the lake?
landscaping.a: We work with the slope instead of against it: walls or terraces to create level spots, beds planted across the grade, paths with steps, and drainage that carries water down in a controlled way. We walk the lot with you first and lay out the options in writing.

flower-bed-installation.q: What ground covers hold a lake slope?
flower-bed-installation.a: Asian jasmine, liriope and monkey grass spread and hold soil well in East Texas, and they handle shade under pines. We plant them in amended soil and mulch them until they fill in.

mulch-installation.q: Why does my mulch keep washing out at the lake?
mulch-installation.a: Slope and water. Hardwood mulch floats and slides off a steep bed in a heavy rain. Pine straw holds better, and an edge on the low side keeps it in. If the bed is taking runoff from above, that needs a drainage fix too.

hardscaping.q: Can you build steps down a Lake Cherokee slope?
hardscaping.a: Yes. We build steps in block or natural stone on a compacted base so they don't shift. Paired with a short wall or terraced beds, they turn a slope you avoid into one you use.

retaining-walls.q: Can a leaning retaining wall be fixed?
retaining-walls.a: Often, yes. On the Lake Cherokee driveway wall we rebuilt in July 2026, we took the block down, compacted a new base and rebuilt it course by course with drainage fabric and pipe behind it. Some walls are too far gone and need a new design, and we'll tell you which after we look.

drainage.q: Where does the water go on a Lake Cherokee drainage job?
drainage.a: Downhill, on a controlled path. We collect runoff from roofs, drives and the slope above, carry it in pipe or a rock-lined swale past the house and walls, and release it lower on the lot slowly enough that it doesn't cut a new gully.

christmas-lights.q: Can you light the lake side of the house?
christmas-lights.a: Yes. We can outline the roofline on the road side, the water side or both. Each side shows up on the photo mock-up we quote from, so you can pick before you book.

irrigation.q: Do you install sprinkler systems at Lake Cherokee?
irrigation.a: Yes. We install and repair sprinkler systems on both the Gregg County and Rusk County sides of the lake, under Texas Licensed Irrigator Matthew Maines, LI0006657. Sloped lake lots get zoned so water soaks in instead of running to the shoreline. Pricing comes after a free walkthrough.
